biggest_catch: The miles have no fixed cash value: 50,000 United miles are worth roughly $550-$600 in flights at typical valuations (about 1.1-1.2 cents per mile), and up to 60,000 if you add an authorized user who makes a purchase. Year-one math: about $550 in flight value with no annual fee in year one leaves roughly $550 net, but the fee is $150 from year two, so decide before then. Only claim this if you were already going to spend $3,000 in 3 months on normal purchases; never spend extra to hit the target. The bonus is unavailable if you currently hold the Explorer or received its new-cardmember bonus in the past 24 months, and Chase's unpublished 5/24 pattern applies.
catches: Only claim this if you were already going to spend the money anyway; never spend extra just to hit the $3,000 minimum, because manufactured spending turns a bonus into debt.

Year-one math: 50,000 miles are worth roughly $550-$600 in flights at typical valuations, minus the $0 first-year fee, which leaves about $550 net. From year two the $150 annual fee applies without a bonus, so keep the card only if your real United flying and perks beat $150 a year. Miles are not cash and devaluation risk is real.

Applying triggers a hard credit inquiry, which typically knocks a few points off your credit score for a short time. Chase also uses its unpublished 5/24 pattern: applicants with five or more newly opened personal cards across any issuer in the last 24 months are generally denied.
This card's APR is around 20% or higher, so carrying a balance would wipe out the bonus fast. Pay the statement balance in full every month or this offer loses you money.
The bonus is not available if you currently have the Explorer card or received a new-cardmember bonus on the Explorer in the past 24 months. Check the current application terms before applying.
Chase's unpublished 5/24 pattern: five or more new personal cards opened in the last 24 months generally means denial, even with excellent credit.

The extra 10,000 miles require adding an authorized user who makes a purchase in the first 3 months, and the miles post to the primary account; the account must be open and not in default when the bonus is paid.

steps: Go to the official Chase United cards page, select Explorer, and read the current offer headline and the Pricing & Terms before anything else.
Confirm your eligibility: you do not currently hold the Explorer and have not received its new-cardmember bonus in the past 24 months.
Apply online. Expect a hard credit inquiry.
Use the card for the purchases you were already planning, totaling at least $3,000 in the first 3 months from account opening.
If you want the extra 10,000 miles, add an authorized user who makes a purchase in the first 3 months.
Pay the statement balance in full every month; do not carry a balance at the ~20%+ APR.
Allow 6-8 weeks after the spending requirement is met for the miles to post, and confirm they appear in your MileagePlus account.
Before the second year's $150 annual fee hits, check whether your real United flying and perks beat $150 a year, and downgrade or cancel if not.
timing: Spend $3,000 on purchases in the first 3 months from account opening. Bonus posts after qualifying purchases, typically 6-8 weeks after the spending requirement is met.
